summary.headline: 100% of the work your services did for these requests was never used.

findings.label: retry_storm
findings.evidence: 3.0 calls per user request and only 0% of the work was used
findings.advice: cap retries with a retry budget (about 10% of traffic), back off with jitter, and stop retrying once the deadline has passed

findings.label: zombie_work
findings.evidence: 66% of the callee's running time happened after the caller had left
findings.advice: send the caller's remaining time to the callee and cancel the work when it passes (deadline propagation)

notes.text: Only 1 user request(s) in this sample. The numbers are exact for it, but too few requests to say what is typical.

These retries were recognised, not read: the same job called the same URL again after a failure. Your client libraries do not mark retries (http.request.resend_count), so a loop that deliberately repeats a failing call would look the same.
No span reports queue wait (attribute app.queue_wait_ms). If your services queue requests before running them, waiting is being counted as work.
